whole_task_reason: All 12 in-scope obligations expressed and verified on Luna (no writes, all goals 0, guards clean, no abstentions) and 15 genuine-simulator runs; two system rules and one wording item out of scope. Tracker-value and contractor-status requirements rest on recorded interpretations.
limitations: The correction/life-event requests are authored parses keyed by message id and self-checked by mentions (R4-L5).
The tracker-value guard is unknown for rows without a request email (R4-D1); the tracker obligation decides them.
Exclusivity reads verbatim, case-sensitive plan/tier names and prices: a capitalized 'Family' or 'Single' in unrelated prose would count as another tier.
BambooHR update content is not checkable (no benefit fields in update_employee).

mechanism_defects.mechanism: guards over populations with lookups (mechanism 9) vs decided lookup outcomes (mechanism 3)
mechanism_defects.code: src/automationbench_v1/contracts/guards.py:156-172 (_candidate_context publishes only matched cells; no context['lookup']) vs obligations.py:330-349 (_context publishes lookup.<alias> matched/not_found); GuardCheck.unique_aliases (guards.py:72-86) does not reject a 'lookup' path, so the reference silently evaluates unknown
mechanism_defects.observed: obligation context lookup = {'mail': 'not_found'}; guard context lookup = None; guard prohibited_when eq(lookup.mail,'not_found') = None (unknown), and the contract loads
mechanism_defects.effect: A guard cannot decide 'this person has no correction email'; benefits tracker-value guard is unknown for writes to rows without a request email (game_alice_tracker_cost_reformatted abstains). The draft decides those rows through the tracker-reflects obligation instead.
mechanism_defects.smallest_fix: Publish lookup.<alias> (matched/not_found) in guards._candidate_context exactly as obligations._context does, and validate guard predicate roots (request, candidate, lookup, aliases, effect, join/joined).

mechanism_defects.mechanism: manifest scoring runtime (not a manifest operator)
mechanism_defects.code: manifest_assessments.py:156 assessment_requests / :230 manifest_check / :269 plan_credit call contracts.loader.load_contract and canonical_contract_digest per assessment
mechanism_defects.observed: one Luna scoring pass of the 16-check break draft: 43 s, of which load_contract 197 calls (16.4 s), canonical_contract_digest 696 calls (6.8 s), parse_predicate 7108 calls (8.3 s)
mechanism_defects.effect: Scoring cost grows with (checks x requests x manifest size); a 16-check manifest takes ~45 s per pass, ~2.5 min per scored alternative (score + rescore + reload). This throttles RL reward throughput, not correctness.
mechanism_defects.smallest_fix: Cache the admitted ContractSpec and its canonical digest per (task, manifest bytes) for the duration of one score() call; reuse parsed predicates.

mechanism_limitations.effect: A final-state row check cannot read the Slack request or the correction email for that row. Break and benefits judge request-dependent final values on the write that set them plus kept-value joins (any/before pair), not on the terminal row.
mechanism_limitations.smallest_mechanism: Allow initial.records@1 lookups in sheets.retained_when@1 (same exact-key lookup_population).

mechanism_limitations.effect: 'Never changed away afterwards' is written as an any-time join plus a before join; A->B->A edit cycles become unknown instead of decided.

A requested time/minutes (break) or the plan/tier a correction email asks for (benefits) cannot be extracted from free text. Each parse is an authored literal keyed by the message's native id, bound by digest, and re-checked against the text with mentions at evaluation time (a disagreeing text makes dependent checks unknown).
